texts.preamble: Nirmala Devi vs Pradeep Chauhan on 13 August, 2025
texts.facts: 2. Plaintiff claims to be the owner of property bearing no. Khasra no. 363, Plot/House no. D-488, situated at Pul Prahladpur, New Delhi- 110044 measuring 50 sq. yards, (hereinafter referred to as "the suit property") residing on the ground floor with her two unmarried sons. Her elder son (Defendant No. 1) and his wife (Defendant No. 2) reside on the second floor as licensees. It is stated that plaintiff purchased the suit property from her husband on 18.07.1995 via General Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sell, Affidavit, and Receipt. The property was constructed with her own earnings and stridhan. Plaintiff and her late husband ran a tea stall "Chauhan Tea Stall" for over 28 years at Shop No. A-8, Opposite D-178, Okhla Phase-I , New Delhi ( hereinafter referred to as "the shop"). The shop was given to the plaintiff and is her only source of livelihood. A separate property at Hari Nagar, Badarpur, was purchased in the name of defendant no.1 but with the joint earnings of the plaintiff and her husband. Defendant no.1 allegedly sold this property without informing the plaintiff. It is claimed that after plaintiff's husband died in 2012. Defendant no.1 began operating the tea stall but stopped supporting the plaintiff financially. Despite repeated requests, he neither vacated the shop nor paid the agreed monthly maintenance of Rs. 5000/- and house rent of Rs.10,000/-, along with arrears of Rs.3,00,000/-. It is claimed that defendant has threatened the plaintiff and her sons, leading to police complaints and publication of a public disownment notice on 11.11.2016. Plaintiff had also filed complaint against defendants before the police vide DD no. 32B dated 31.10.2017. Thereafter, plaintiff sent a legal notice dated 31.12.2017 to the defendant to vacate the suit property. Basement of the suit property is being used by the brother of defendant no.1 for running his coaching centre. Plaintiff and brother of defendant no.1 are residing on the ground floor whereas one brother is residing in first floor in one room. Two rooms of the first floor and one room of the second floor are rented out by the plaintiff and also two room of third floor of the property have been rented out by the plaintiff to the tenants. Defendant no.1 claims that he had been running a shop bearing no. A-8, Opp. D-178, Okhla, Phase- I, New Delhi, with his father under the name and style of Chauhan Tea Stall. Certified copy of Ex.PW-1/11 registration certificate dated 25.02.2016 issued by Department of Labour Government of NCT of Delhi filed in CS SCJ 13. Certified copy of Aadhar Ex.PW-1/15 Card filed in CS SCJ 9. PW-1 was cross-examined at length and plaintiff's evidence was closed on 01.03.2025. He relied upon the following documents: - SL Documents Exhibits 1 Copy of registration Ex.DW1/1 certificate of the tea stall (OSR) being run in the name of Chauhan Tea Stall dated 25.02.2016 issued by Department of Labour 2 Copy of registration Ex.DW1/2 certificate dated 04.08.2017 (colly) issued by Delhi (OSR) Government, Department of Food Safety in respect of Tea Stall at Shop no. 48, Near D-178, Okhla Phase-I, yashu khurana khurana Date: 2025.08.13 16:20:43 +0530 CS SCJ 848/18 NIRMALA DEVI Vs. PRADEEP CHAUHAN Page no. 8 of 16 New Delhi. 3 Copy of Tax receipt dated Ex.DW1/3 21.05.2018 issued by MCD, (OSR) Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi- 110024 4 Copies of electricity bills Ex.DW1/4 dated 17.10.2018 and (colly) 18.11.2018 11. DW-1 was cross- examined at length and discharged on 27.05.2025. Thereafter, defendant no.2 i.e. DW-2 Ms. Pooja Chauhan, tendered her evidence by way of affidavit i.e. Ex.DW-2/A, wherein, she majorly reiterated the contents of the written statement. Hence, for the brevity of the decision, the same is not being reiterated. She has not relied upon any documents. She was cross-examined and discharged and defendant's evidence was closed on 13.06.2025. Subsequently, the matter was fixed for final arguments. Both the issues pertain to the shop, hence, they are taken up collectively. 14. The onus of proving the issues was cast upon the plaintiff. To discharge the onus of prove, plaintiff contended that the shop bearing no. D-178, Okha Phase-I, New Delhi- 110020 , was purchased by her late husband namely Lalit Singh Chauhan and after his death, defendant no.1 has been in possession of the said shop. Defendant no.1 has been running a business of tea stall at the said shop and plaintiff claims a declaration, permanent and mandatory injunction against the defendants, thereby directing them to remove all articles from the shop and hand over possession of the shop to the plaintiff. Plaintiff has also relied upon Ex.PW-1/4 (OSR) i.e. copy of the newspaper "Veer Arjun" dated 11.11.2016, whereby plaintiff had disowned defendant no.1 as her son, by way of publication. Plaintiff claims that after demise of her late husband, plaintiff has no right to remain in the shop. Therefore, she is entitled to reliefs claimed in prayer no. 1 and 3 of the plaint. Based on the aforesaid document, plaintiff claims ownership over the suit property. It is claimed that defendants are residing as licensee in one room on second floor of the suit property. It is claimed that the license was terminated by the plaintiff vide notice dated 12.12.2017. However, defendants have failed to vacate the suit property, hence, plaintiff is entitled to the reliefs claimed in Nirmala Devi vs Pradeep Chauhan on 13 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126152375/ 8 prayer clause (ii) of the plaint. 20. Per contra, defendants claim that Ex.PW-1/2 (colly) (OSR) i.e. copy of general power of attorney, agreement to sell, affidavit and receipts, dated 13.07.1995, do not confer any right, title or interest to the plaintiff in the suit property.
